title: The Buddha Dal Refuses to Quit Doaba

blocks.text: Bishambhar Dass answers the Sikh demand with defiance, saying ransom will be paid only if the entire Khalsa speaks with one voice and only after the Buddha Dal withdraws. The Singhs reject that posture by recalling that Dina Beg had an agreement with the Singhs, so Bishambhar has no right to pose as if he alone can rewrite the terms of the region.

With negotiation hardening into challenge, both sides are pushed toward a test of nerve. The page stresses that neither camp is willing to budge, and that questions of alliance, honour, and coercion have become inseparable from the coming battle.

Emboldened by numbers and support from hill chiefs, Bishambhar moves against a Sikh force that is scattered and comparatively thin on the ground. Even so, the Singhs prepare themselves for the fight instead of retreating from the claim they have made in Doaba.
